issue.body:
Modifies `BlobStoreRepository.ShardBlobsToDelete.shardDeleteResults` to have a variable size depending on the remaining heap space rather than a hard-coded 2GB size which caused smaller nodes with less heap space to OOMe.

Relates to #131822
Closes #116379

Closes ES-12540

issue.body:
Skip unnecessary loading of `IndexMetadata` during snapshot deletion

During snapshot deletion we load the metadata for an index into heap purely to calculate the shard count. On nodes with small heaps, loading multiple objects concurrently can cause them to OOMe.

Rather than recomputing the shard count value for the same index across multiple snapshots, this change stores the shard count in a map. This stops loading multiple IndexMetaData objects into heap for the same index.

This means that for commands such as:
```
assertAcked(client().admin().cluster().prepareDeleteSnapshot(timeout, repoName, snapshotName1, snapshotName2).get())
```
assuming both snapshots include Index1, we only loaded Index1's metadata once.

For commands such as:
```
assertAcked(client().admin().cluster().prepareDeleteSnapshot(timeout, repoName, snapshotName1).get())
assertAcked(client().admin().cluster().prepareDeleteSnapshot(timeout, repoName, snapshotName2).get())
```
since these are different delete snapshot requests, we load Index1's metadata once for each

Relates to: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/131822

Closes ES-12539

<!--

---

As a note, I did consider an alternative approach. 

We currently load the index metadata [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/repositories/blobstore/BlobStoreRepository.java#L1855) inside the `finalizeSnapshot` method. Since the number of primary shards does not change for an index, we could store the shard count here instead (moving the `indexUUIDToShardCountMap` up to the `BlobStoreRepository` level rather than `SnapshotDeletion`). Then, when deleting snapshots, the `IndexMetaData` would not need to be loaded at all.

There were however two issues with this:
1. The `indexUUIDToShardCountMap` map would grow every time an index was added, so clusters adding thousands of indices would quickly grow this map, and there would need to be some form of clean up logic added.
2. If the repository is deleted, then this map does not exist. Therefore I would still need to modify the `determineShardCount` as shown in this PR. 

The benefit is that both commands
```
assertAcked(client().admin().cluster().prepareDeleteSnapshot(timeout, repoName, snapshotName1, snapshotName2).get())
assertAcked(client().admin().cluster().prepareDeleteSnapshot(timeout, repoName, snapshotName2).get())
```
would not load *any* index metadata into heap, assuming the repository was not deleted.

This would also implicitly close ES-12538 since we would no longer have any concurrency concerns
-->

issue.body:
Replaces the existing `ChecksumBlobStoreFormat` `INDEX_METADATA_FORMAT` inside `BlobStoreRepository` with a new `INDEX_SHARD_COUNT_FORMAT`. This removes the need for writing an entire `IndexMetadata` object to, and reading from, heap memory. Instead, we write to and read from heap only the shard count for an index, reducing the total heap memory needed for snapshotting and reducing the likelihood a node will go OOMe.

Relates to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/131822
Relates to ES-12539
Closes ES-12538

body:
This issue had 3 main tasks:
1. Limit the size of `shardDeleteResults` which was completed by https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/133558
2. Skip unnecessarily loading `IndexMetadata` which had the PR https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/134441 to solve, but was closed due to the benefits of:
3. Limiting the concurrency of snapshot deletions on nodes with small heap. This was resolved by https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/137210 reducing the heap allocations required during snapshot deletion from an entire `IndexMetadata` object which could be upwards of 50MB to requiring only an integer. There are no concurrency concerns with this smaller allocation requirement, and so all nodes will continue to have upwards of ten concurrent snapshot deletion threads. The performance benefit of this change also resolved point 2 above
